title: Can the multinomial theorem be proved as a generalization of the binomial theorem?

problemStatement.formal: theorem multinomial_theorem {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R] (s : Finset α) (f : α → R) (n : ℕ) : (∑ i ∈ s, f i) ^ n = ∑ k ∈ s.piAntidiag n, (Nat.multinomial s k : R) * ∏ i ∈ s, f i ^ k i
problemStatement.plain: The multinomial theorem: expanding (∑ f(i))^n gives a weighted sum over all exponent distributions k:s→ℕ with ∑k=n, weighted by multinomial coefficients. The binomial theorem is the special case |s|=2.
whyMatters: Establishes the formal connection between multinomial and binomial theorems
Proves the multinomial theorem for arbitrary commutative semirings over finite index sets
Shows the inductive structure: binomial theorem drives the multinomial induction

proven: multinomial_recurrence: multinomial(insert a s, k) = C(k(a)+Σk, k(a)) · multinomial(s,k)
multinomial_eq_binomial: For 2-element sets, multinomial = binomial coefficient
multinomial_bool_form_eq_binomial: Bool-indexed multinomial equals classical binomial expansion

insights: Mathlib's Finset.sum_pow_eq_sum_piAntidiag is the key lemma - it IS the multinomial theorem

Key proof fix: 'fun b => if b then y else x' reduces definitionally for Bool (false→x, true→y) via rfl, avoiding Bool equality issues with 'if b = false then x else y'
piAntidiag s n is the finset of all functions k:s→ℕ with ∑k=n
